Calculate the length of the side $x$, giving your answer to two decimal places.

current_example.problem:
Consider the following triangle:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14249653/assets/9fbf9672296b128a16336120999c2c836d950fda32154bc7a0f0a91b0e8799e6.png)

Calculate the length of the side $a,$ giving your answer to the nearest tenth.
current_example.worked_solution:
The Law of Cosines states that

$$
a^2 = b^2+c^2-2bc\cos{A}.
$$

Here, we have

$$
m\angle A = 75^{\circ},\quad b = 10,\quad c=9.
$$

Substituting the numbers into the formula gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2} & ={10}^{2}+{9}^{2}-2(10)(9)\operatorname{cos}⁡{75}^{∘} \\  & =100+81-180\operatorname{cos}⁡{75}^{∘} \\  & =181-180\cdot 0.258\text{ }8… \\  & =181-46.587\text{ }4… \\  & =134.412\text{ }6\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $4$ decimal places

Taking the square root gives

$$
a = \sqrt{134.4126} = 11.6
$$

to the nearest tenth.
